name: ANSI wired-AND connection
summary: Several open-collector outputs joined on one pulled-up line, so any output pulling low makes the line low.
description: A wired-AND connection is formed by joining open-collector or open-drain outputs to a single line with one pull-up. The line is high only when every output is off, so in positive logic the result is the AND of the individual output states. Some schematics draw a small AND outline around the junction to make the implied function visible.

Shared interrupt lines, ready signals and I2C-style buses rely on this arrangement. A drawing should show every output on the net, the single pull-up, and the supply, because adding or removing a driver changes the logic and the pull-up current.
The connection only works with open-circuit outputs. Joining push-pull outputs in the same way causes contention and possible damage, so the output type of each gate must be checked.
readingNotes: Check that every joined output is open collector or open drain.
There should be one pull-up for the whole net.
drawingChecklist: Show all contributing outputs on the shared net.
Draw a single pull-up with its value and supply.
Mark the open-circuit output type on each driver.
distinction: A wired-OR uses open-emitter outputs with a pull-down; wired-AND uses open-collector outputs with a pull-up.
